mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Wednesday 4:07 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-11 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Capricor Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Develops cell and exosome therapies, led by deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.why: Shares jumped about 26% as traders positioned for the FDA's decision on deramiocel, due by Nov 22 after a three-month extension. A Stocktwits news piece says investors are reading hints about possible label wording; an FDA advisory panel voted 9-3 against the drug's efficacy evidence in July, so the outcome is uncertain.

items.name: RUM Group Inc.
items.about: Runs the Rumble video platform and Quake AI, a GPU cloud business.
items.why: The parent of Rumble reported record Q3 revenue of $96.6M, up 290% from a year earlier and above the ~$89M consensus, with its Quake AI cloud unit contributing $68.2M at about a 34% adjusted EBITDA margin. It also posted its first positive adjusted EBITDA; the stock rose about 16%.

items.name: Figure Technology Solutions Inc
items.about: Runs a blockchain-based platform for home-equity loans and other consumer credit.
items.why: The stock rose about 3.5% ahead of Q3 results expected Thursday, Nov 12, with consensus around $250M in revenue, up roughly 60% on the year. Shares had fallen about 31% since the last report, and posts point to late call buying into the print.

items.name: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing sonelokimab for inflammatory skin and joint diseases.
items.why: Shares climbed about 7.6% in a move posts describe as a technical breakout; no new company announcement was found. Calendars list the next quarterly report around Nov 17, and the stock remains far below levels before its 2025 Phase 3 setback.

items.name: Amprius Technologies Inc
items.about: Makes high-energy-density silicon-anode lithium-ion batteries for drones and aviation.
items.why: Q3 revenue hit a record $39.1M, up 83% from a year earlier and above the ~$35.8M estimate, and the 2026 target was raised to at least $140M. Even so, the stock fell about 6.7% the day after the report, and posts are split between frustration and calls that the selloff is overdone.

items.name: Aurinia Pharmaceuticals Inc
items.about: Sells Lupkynis, a treatment for lupus nephritis, and develops immunology drugs.
items.why: Shares slipped about 0.5% on a quiet day while the biotech index rose; no new company news was found. It ranks on the board largely because of its big, active Stocktwits following, and chatter this week has been above its monthly average.

items.name: CoreWeave Inc
items.about: Rents out GPU-based cloud computing capacity for AI training and inference.
items.why: CoreWeave jumped about 25% after Q3 revenue rose 168% to $3.66B, beating estimates, with a $132.5B backlog and 2026 revenue guidance raised to $13.0–13.3B. Benzinga said the report helped add about $500B to tech stock values, and analysts at Citi and Goldman kept Buy ratings.

items.name: SPDR Gold Shares ETF
items.about: ETF that holds physical gold bullion.
items.why: GLD fell about 1.1% as gold slipped under $4,000 an ounce. Higher Treasury yields and rising bets on a December Fed rate hike lifted the US dollar to its highest in more than a year, which weighs on gold.

items.name: Clorox Co.
items.about: Makes household cleaning and consumer products, including Clorox bleach and Purell.
items.why: Clorox swung between about $102 and $110 and ended up 0.5%, after rising about 14% over the prior five sessions. Posts say there is takeover interest, including from European investors, but no report or company statement confirming any approach was found.

items.name: Revolution Medicines Inc
items.about: Develops RAS-targeted cancer drugs for pancreatic, lung and colorectal tumours.
items.why: The stock fell about 6.2% to a new intraday low near $180; no company news explaining the drop was found. Posts list analyst targets from $179 to $350 and note it trades about 20% below its August high of $224.

items.name: Nebius Group N.V.
items.about: Netherlands-based AI cloud provider offering GPU clusters and AI services.
items.why: Shares rose about 15.5% alongside CoreWeave, as peer results lifted AI-cloud stocks. Nebius reports Q3 results Thursday, Nov 12, with a call at 8:00 AM ET, and posts are positioning for that report.

items.name: Verizon Communications Inc.
items.about: US wireless and broadband telecom carrier.
items.why: Verizon edged up about 0.6% on unusually heavy volume as some money moved into defensive dividend stocks. Bearish posts point to its large debt load (over $130B) at a time of rising Fed rate-hike bets.

items.name: Strategy
items.about: Software firm that mainly holds bitcoin on its balance sheet as a treasury asset.
items.why: Shares rose about 1.1%, but the crowd is very bearish ahead of MSCI's November index review. New MSCI rules finalized in October could exclude companies like Strategy whose assets are mostly bitcoin, and posts argue over what removal would mean.

items.name: Fervo Energy Co
items.about: Develops enhanced geothermal power plants, including projects in Utah.
items.why: Shares jumped about 14% as power suppliers to data centers rallied with the AI trade. Posts point to a recently reported record-hot Utah test well and earlier Google power deals; no new company announcement was found today.

items.name: DESTINY TECH 100 INC
items.about: Closed-end fund holding stakes in private tech companies such as SpaceX and AI firms.
items.why: The fund slipped about 1.2% as traders weighed what happens to private-company proxies once those companies list. Posts cite a Nasdaq notice that Anthropic's shares are set to begin trading Nov 19 and recall that DXYZ fell after SpaceX went public.

items.name: SoFi Technologies Inc
items.about: Online bank and lender offering loans, deposits and investing.
items.why: SoFi dipped about 0.6% while the major indexes rose, and posts complain the stock is giving back its post-earnings gap. No new company news was found; it trends partly because of its very large Stocktwits following.

items.name: Adobe Inc
items.about: Makes creative and document software including Photoshop, Premiere and Acrobat.
items.why: Adobe was little changed, up about 0.3%, but sentiment is bearish after Citi cut it to Sell with a $207 target on Nov 4, the third downgrade in about three weeks. Posts argue AI tools threaten its software business; fiscal 2027 guidance comes with its December report.

items.name: Energy Fuels Inc
items.about: US producer of uranium and rare-earth elements, with a Utah processing mill.
items.why: Shares rose about 2.7% as posts discussed North American rare-earth supply, including a Ucore feedstock delivery, and long-term magnet demand. No new Energy Fuels announcement was found.

items.name: Ondas Inc
items.about: Makes autonomous drone systems and private industrial wireless networks.
items.why: The stock rose about 3.1% ahead of Q3 results due Thursday, Nov 12 before an 8:30 AM ET call. Management guided Q3 revenue to $140–155M; posts note heavy volume into the close and say short interest is high.

items.name: GE Vernova Inc.
items.about: Makes gas turbines, wind turbines and grid equipment for power producers.
items.why: GE Vernova rose about 1.6% but gave back an early climb above $840. Posts debate reports that SoftBank scaled back turbine orders for an Ohio data-center power project; posts say a breakage fee was paid, but neither company has confirmed. A Nov 9 TIKR analysis said even the full Ohio plan would be a small slice of GE Vernova's gas-equipment backlog.
